blocks.text: **The task.** Given an array and a number `k`, find the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of exactly `k` elements.
Textbook fixed window. Build the first `k` elements, then slide, tracking the best sum seen.
Four windows, and after the first each took one addition and one subtraction. The brute force would have summed three elements four times — twelve additions instead of six.
`if (arr.length < k) return null;` matters. Without it, the build loop reads past the end of the array and quietly produces a wrong answer from `undefined` values rather than failing loudly.
**Time: O(N)** — every element enters the window once and leaves at most once.
**Space: O(1)** — one running sum and one best.
Brute force would be O(N x k). For a million elements and k of a thousand, that is a billion operations versus a million.
